speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: Allow me to elaborate on the two key legislative changes contained in the Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) is empowered under the MPA Act to regulate the provision of marine and port services and facilities in Singapore, including the two cruise terminals – the Singapore Cruise Centre (SCC) and Marina Bay Cruise Centre Singapore (MBCCS).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: For cruise services, MPA oversees maritime safety and security as well as the pricing of port services and facilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: MPA and STB also jointly regulate berth allocations and service standards of the terminal operators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: This is sensible as these factors are vital to the implementation of our cruise tourism industry, which STB oversees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: Under clause 5 of the Bill, we are now formalising and clarifying STB's regulatory role over the cruise terminal operators in the Singapore Tourism Board Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: Singapore's cruise tourism industry has grown tremendously since the opening of MBCCS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: Despite the COVID-19 pandemic, demand for cruise holidays has rebounded strongly worldwide.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: The Cruise Lines International Association projected that global cruise passenger volume will recover to pre-pandemic levels by the end of this year and increase by approximately 30%, compared to 2019, by 2026.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: With a low market penetration rate of 0.2%, the cruise industry is especially optimistic about the growth potential in the Asia Pacific region.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: As the volume of cruise tourism grows, Singapore's cruise terminals will become critical infrastructure for our tourism sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: The newly added Part 3AA in the Bill provides clarity on the cruise terminal licensing regime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: New sections such as sections 32A and 32B further empower STB to conduct surveys and obtain information such as financial and operational data from the cruise terminal licensees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: Such data will help STB monitor the industry's development and make comprehensive analyses and projections for effective economic regulation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: As cruise terminals are international gateways into Singapore with significant market power, sections 29R and 29S empower STB to have oversight and control over the ownership and acquisition of the cruise terminal licensees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: The intent is not to control the day-to-day commercial decisions of the licensees but where there are material changes to the equity control of the licensee, STB's approval will be required to safeguard Singapore's national interests.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: Section 29V also requires the cruise terminal licensees' central management and control to be ordinarily exercised within Singapore so that STB can take enforcement action swiftly if any contraventions ever arise.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: Section 29ZB provides for a special administration order to be made, where the affairs, business and property of the cruise terminal licensee may be managed directly by STB.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: These powers are intended to ensure business continuity and avoid disruptions of cruise operations and passenger flows under extraordinary circumstances, such as the insolvency of a terminal operator.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: In drafting these amendments, close references were made to similar provisions in the MPA Act, as well as the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) Act, which exercises similar powers over Singapore’s airports.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: STB will exercise these powers with a light touch, with the primary goals of: one, growing the cruise industry to benefit our economy and, two, strengthening Singapore’s position as the region’s leading cruise hub.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: We have also consulted stakeholders in the cruise industry and have incorporated their feedback accordingly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: Consequential amendments will be made to the MPA Act to avoid any overlaps in the regulation of cruise terminal operators when STB takes over the roles I have just described.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: All other marine and port services and facilities will continue to be regulated by MPA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: STB and MPA will work closely to ensure the seamless implementation of these amendments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: The second set of changes clarifies and enhances STB’s administrative capabilities and enforcement powers over the broader tourism industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: First, clauses 3 and 4 of the Bill introduce administrative amendments to update and incorporate flexibility into the Board’s voting processes, tenure and the number of members.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: This is in line with the Board provisions for other Statutory Boards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: Second, clause 6 of the Bill clarifies STB’s purview over tourism enterprises and expressly provides for powers to provide grants and act as guarantor for selected strategic tourism enterprises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: Third, clause 11 of the Bill accords legal recognition to the electronic version of tourist guide badges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: This will allow tourist guides to access their badges more conveniently online.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: Both physical and electronic badges will continue to be recognised, until a transition to a full e-licensing regime takes place at an appropriate time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: Fourth, clause 21 of the Bill expressly provides for the power of the Board to collect and access tourism information reasonably required for the functions and duties of STB, including industry development and promotion.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: Singapore’s tourism sector is poised for strong growth as it emerges from the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: This Bill will enable STB to drive the development and regulation of our tourism sector more effectively and continue its efforts to make Singapore an attractive tourism destination for all.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This will enable STB to exercise regulatory oversight of financial matters in a manner that supports the growth and development of the cruise sector and in turn, Singapore’s tourism sector.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first point is on the new section 8HA.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: STB may end up propping up mismanaged, decaying businesses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: STB may also be accused of picking and choosing winners in the tourism industry, unfairly disadvantaging those not lucky enough to be chosen.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This power should thus be used in extremely limited situations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The decision to use it must be guided by clear, objective frameworks of success.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: How will the Minister decide whether to approve instances where STB seek to use this power?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In what situations is STB envisioned to use this power?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second point is about how public interest will be determined under the amended Act.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A number of amendments proposed refer to the STB or Controller making decisions on the basis of “public interest”.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One example is the STB’s power in granting or renewing tourist guide licences to impose conditions that are in the public interest.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The STB may also give licensees directions that are necessary or expedient in the public interest.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I ask this because “public interest” is not a term that is currently used in the Singapore Tourism Board Act.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, the term is repeatedly used in this Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My third point is on how STB will assist the cruise line industry in reaching its sustainability goals.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Concerns have been raised about the carbon emissions, pollution and significant energy demands of cruises.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Earlier this year, the Friends of the Earth, an NGO, evaluated 18 cruise lines according to four environmental criteria.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: No cruise line got better than a C grade.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The report card concluded that “clean cruising” was simply not possible.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Research suggests that a large cruise ship can have a carbon footprint of greater than 12,000 cars.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That is twice the number of cars newly registered in Singapore every year.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Singapore Green Plan 2030 aims for our nation to become a sustainable tourist destination.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MPA has also said it aims to decarbonise the maritime industry.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What steps will STB take to help decarbonise the cruise line industry?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What targets will it set, and on what specific areas does it aim to drive reduced emissions?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For instance, are there goals for cruises to transition first to using liquefied natural gas and subsequently to other low or zero-carbon marine fuels?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Notwithstanding these clarifications, I stand in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the introduction of a new provision for STB to act as a guarantor for tourism enterprises and the situations in which STB might do so.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Multiple layers of safeguards will be in place before STB takes on this guarantor role.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For example, a comprehensive risk assessment will be conducted to measure factors such as: (a) the risk to the Government; (b) the track record of the tourism enterprise, (c) potential cost and time savings; and (d) economic benefits.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: STB will also need to seek the approvals of its Board of Directors as well as the Minister for Trade and Industry.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Additional safeguards may also be taken to reduce the overall risk to STB, such as requesting indemnity from the tourism enterprise.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked how public interest will be determined in this Bill.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The term “public interest” appears in legislation of other regulatory regimes, such as in the Travel Agents Act 1975.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As I mentioned in my speech, the cruise terminals are international gateways into Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As a port of entry, there are safety and security considerations on whether the cruise terminal licensee is fit and proper to operate such a critical checkpoint.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Where there are risks to Singapore’s public interest, for example, being complicit in allowing a breach of border security, the Controller will be able to take into consideration these factors to assess the suitability of the licensee.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Other factors which may be taken into account include, but are not limited to, public health considerations.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For example, in a public health emergency, cruise terminal and tourist guide licensees may be directed to abide by new protocols in relation to persons at cruise terminals or in their tour groups, so as to protect the general well-being of the public.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Just like other regulatory regimes, STB and the Controller will ensure there is clear public interest involved before relying on this ground.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: With regards to the sustainability efforts of the cruise sector, which Mr Louis Ng asked about, the global cruise industry’s commitment to environmental sustainability is evident.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Liquefied natural gas (LNG) is one of the cleanest-burning non-electric marine fuels available today.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: There is an increasing trend of cruise lines building LNG-powered ships.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This is a significant step as the use of LNG results in almost no sulphur emissions, reduces nitrogen oxide emissions by 85% and reduces greenhouse gas emissions by 20%.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The industry is also actively exploring the use of alternative sustainable fuels and implementing them at scale in future.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In April this year, the Cruise Lines International Association (CLIA) announced clear commitments to implement environmentally sustainable practices at sea and at berths.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In line with our Singapore Green Plan 2030, Singapore is well-positioned to facilitate the cruise industry’s shift towards a more sustainable future.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As a leading bunkering hub with expertise in ancillary services, such as the retrofitting of LNG ships, we are an ideal homeport for LNG-powered ships.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: STB’s grant schemes also encourage the deployment of cruise ships with sustainable practices to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In 2022, Singapore will welcome its first deployment of an LNG-powered cruise ship, Silversea’s Silver Nova.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This will pave the way for the deployment of more sustainably powered cruise ships to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I wish to thank Mr Louis Ng for his questions and keen support for this Bill, which will be critical for our tourism industry.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We look forward to the continued support of this House in this endeavour.
